questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

You don’t have to invest (1)/ on an fancy camera if you’re (2)/ not a photography buff. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: In the above sentence, the article ‘an’ has been wrongly used before the word fancy. Since the article, ‘an’ can only be used before words that start with vowel or vowel sounds. Therefore the correct article use is, ‘on **a fancy** camera’. Therefore, part 2 of the sentence is wrong.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

We accept unbelievably low rates for (1)/ sponsored articles; (2)/ a "something is better than nothing" kind of attitude. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The sentence is both meaningfully and grammatically correct. Therefore, it has no error.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

For candidates with work-experience, interviewer (1)/ questions about their company, test the depth of their knowledge (2)/ and understandings of the immediate environment. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: In part 3 of the sentence, the word ‘understandings’ has been used in the plural form. This is incorrect. Whenever referring to a subject, the use of the word understanding before ‘of’ should be done in singular. Thus, the correct phrase will be ‘and understanding of the immediate environment’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Agent Chitrangada will telegraphed a secret (1)/ code word to her boss as part (2)/ of a dubious mission. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution: The use of the verb ‘telegraph’ has been wrongly done in the first part of the sentence. Since the sentence is in simple future tense, the form of the verb ‘telegraphed’, which is simple past tense, should be replaced with ‘telegraph’ which is simple future tense. So, the correction is ‘Agent Chitrangada **will telegraph **a secret’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

You have too save the day by (1)/ cracking the code and (2)/ determining the code word. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: 'Too’ means also, whereas ‘to’ is a preposition (used for expressing a point). Here the word ‘too’ has been incorrectly used in place of ‘to’. The correct way to phrase the sentence will be ‘You **have to **save the day by’.

**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Hard as it is to believe, (1)/ she has no formal education also (2)/ training in content at all. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: In the second part of the sentence, the use of the word conjunction ‘also’ needs to be replaced with the conjunction ‘or’ for the sentence to be meaningful. The correct way to write is 'Hard as it is to believe, she has no **formal education or training **in content at all.'

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I also used to write scripts for hosting school (1)/ functions. Though, on that time I (2)/ hadn’t identified this interest. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: The preposition ‘on’ is not used to indicate time. Thus correct preposition that should be used in the second part of the sentence is ‘at’. questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Either she or her friends **(have planning)** to come here.
questions.solution:
The helping verb ‘have’ has been wrongly used in the above sentence. Whenever there is the use of either-or, both the subjects have to be considered while determining the helping verb. 

Thus, the correct sentence will be **‘either she or her friends are planning to come here’.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

**(I, you and she)** are the best brains here.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'you, she and I'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The order of the personal pronouns ‘I, you, and she’ should be replaced by ‘you, she and I’ 
 
• For good and positive statements, the order is Second, Third, and First-person.
 
• For example:
 
 
• *You, he, and I had gone shopping.*
 
• *You, she, and I were best friends.*
 
 
 
• The given sentence expresses a positive thought of making her understand, hence, the order of the personal pronouns should be changed.

**The correct sentence is: *Y****ou, she, and I are the best brains here.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

She has worked **(really hardly)** and has no issues with fitness or her game.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__really hard__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An adverb can be defined: A word or phrase that modifies or qualifies an adjective, verb, or other adverb or a word group__, expressing a relation of place, time, circumstance, manner, cause, degree, etc. (example, gently, quite, then, there).
 
• Here, replace '__*hardly*__' with '*hard*'.
 
• '*Hardly*' denotes barely or scarcely, whereas '*hard*' means '__*firm/ tough*__'.
 
• Observe the difference in the use of 'hard' and 'hardly',
 
• Example: *He works hard*.
 
• Example: *He hardly works*. (means “*He barely works*.”)
 
 
• We don't say: *This hardly-won supremacy was not to be lost*.
 
• We say: *This hard-won supremacy was not to be lost*.
 
 

Correct sentence: *She has worked** really hard** and has no issues with fitness or her game.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

I have _______ milk to drink.
questions.solution: **Milk is not a countable noun**, thus, 'many' cannot be used here. 'Most' can only be used in a **comparative sense. **Since there is no comparison being made here, this option is also not correct. '**Enough' means 'adequate' **which makes the sentence meaningful. Therefore, the correct sentence is ‘I have enough milk to drink’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

There were trees on ______ side of the road.
questions.solution:
If the meaning that is to be expressed is that no trees were there, then ‘**neither side’ **would be used but **not ‘no side’. **

Further, 'any' is used to refer to a part, thus it is not appropriate here. Finally, either means both, which is conveying the intended meaning. Thus, the correct sentence is ‘there were trees on either side of the road.’

Decoy
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 3) **Trap**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Decoy'** refers to a person, thing, or situation that is used to lure or entice someone into a trap or to divert attention from the real intention or target. (जाल)

 
 
• **Example:** The hunters used a duck decoy to attract real ducks into the trap.

• **Example: **The police set up a decoy to trap the suspect into revealing himself.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is- **3) Trap**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example: **The thief attempted to steal jewelry from the house.
 
 
 
• **Foil - **This verb means to prevent something considered wrong or undesirable from succeeding. It usually implies a direct opposition or thwarting of plans. (Hindi meaning: नाकाम बनाना)
 
 
• **Example: **The detective foiled the villain's plot at the last minute.
 
 
 
• **Attempt -** This noun or verb denotes an act of trying to achieve something, often something difficult or with uncertain outcomes. (Hindi meaning: प्रयास)
 
 
• **Example: **After several attempts, she finally succeeded in breaking the record.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Stress is a

P: lot of people because

Q: of the day to day labour

R: major concern for a
questions.solution:
The correct order of the sentence is RPQ.

After stress is ‘a’; neither ‘lot of people’ nor ‘of’ can follow. Therefore, the first sentence has to be R. Similarly ‘a’ cannot be followed by ‘of’. So, the next correct sentence is P. Finally the only option left is Q. Thus the correct sentence by elimination is 'Stress is a major concern for a lot of people because of the day to day labour'.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

When the 

P: our country was

Q: economically backward

R: Britishers left
questions.solution:
The correct order of the sentence is RPQ.

After when the, there should be a subject, which is given by R i.e. ‘the Britishers’. Then, it must be followed by the body of the sentence i.e. O ‘our country was’. Finally, it must be concluded by the final remark on the state of the country i.e. Q ‘economically backward’. Thus the correct sentence is **‘When the Britishers left, our country was economically backward’.**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Global warming

P: is the steady and

Q: level of earth's temperature

R: continuous rise in the
questions.solution: The correct order of the sentence is PRQ. Global warming is defined in the sentence so the first following part should start with ‘is’ i.e. P. After ‘Global warming is the steady **and’ **there should be another adjective i.e. continuous (R) and finally it should be followed by the concluding phrase i.e. Q. Thus the correct sentence is **‘Global warming is the steady and continuous rise in the level of earth's temperature.’**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Education is

P: for acquiring

Q: skills and law knowledge

R: an important medium
questions.solution: The correct order of the sentence is RPQ. 'Education is' should be followed by an explanatory connector. Out of the given options, it is R ‘an important medium’. Further, a verb should follow i.e. P (for acquiring) and finally the concluding remark i.e. Q (skills and knowledge). Therefore, the correct order of the sentence is **‘Education is an important medium for acquiring skills and law knowledge’.**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Good health is

P: happiness during his life time

Q: healthy man can enjoy great

R: important because a
questions.solution:
The correct order is RQP.

‘Good health is’ should be followed by an explanatory phrase i.e. R (important because). Then, the body including the word should follow i.e. Q (healthy man can **enjoy**). Finally, the concluding remark should follow i.e. P (happiness during his lifetime). Thus the correct sentence is **‘Good health is important because a healthy man can enjoy great happiness during his lifetime’.**

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Nisha has rung the bell.

options.text: The bell has been rung by Nisha.
The bell was being rung by Nisha.
The bell was rung by Nisha.
The bell has being rung by Nisha.

questions.solution: In a change from active voice (Subject + Verb + Object) to passive voice (Object + Verb + Subject), the verb also changes. The simple present perfect form of the verb will become past perfect. Therefore, the passive voice will be 'The bell **has been **rung by Nisha.' Thus, the correct answer is option 1.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dbd70ea3a020b879b11334d2851ddd8dbc9b8a39e2f5af5675278c35a1f54f8d.png] ****Explanation**

The given sentence is in the direct mode of narration. The reporting verb is in the simple past tense and there are three different verbs in the reported speech in two different tenses- 'have been'(present perfect), I am (simple present) and thanks ie. (I) thank you(simple present).

When we convert this particular sentence from the direct to the indirect mode of narration, we have to make the following changes:

 
• Since the** reporting verb** is in the** simple past tense**, all the** verbs in the reported speech** will undergo a **backshift of tense**:
 
• Present perfect** 'have been'** is changed into past perfect** 'had been'**
 
• Simple present** 'I am'** is changed into simple past** 'I was'**
 
• Simple present** 'thank' **is changed into simple past** 'thanked'**
 
• **'Now'** is changed to** 'then'**

**​**Following these steps here we find that the correct sentence is **Option 4 **which is the correct answer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/857d4045d25cda3d10da810cea7d7b369ce1feb23b82dcae175067292470a7b3.png] **Points to note**

When we convert a sentence from direct to indirect speech, we make the following changes:

 
• **Quotation marks** are **omitted** and the sentence** ends with a full stop**. 
 
• The **tense** of the **verb**, in the reported speech involving any **order, request and instruction** does** not undergo** any **change **during the conversion from direct to indirect mode. This is also true if the statement is a** universal truth.** 
 
• If the** reporting verb** is in the **present tense**, it does **not undergo** any **change**.
 
• We add the word** 'to' **before the verb if the verb is in the **bare infinitive**.
 
• When the reporting or **principal verb** is in the **present tense**, all present tenses of the direct are **changed** into the corresponding** past tenses.**
 
• Words expressing **nearness in time or place** are generally converted into words expressing** distance**. For eg.** now** becomes **then**,** today** becomes **that day**, **yesterday** becomes **the previous day**, **this** becomes** that** etc.
 
• In reporting **commands and requests**, the** verb expressing command or request **is **added** and the** imperative **is changed into the** infinitive.** 
 
• In reporting** questions** the** verbs** like** asked inquired** are **added** 
 
• In reporting** exclamations and wishes**, the** verbs expressing exclamation or wish** are **added**. 
 
• When we convert a sentence from the direct to the indirect mode(especially for a sentence** ending** with a** mark of interrogation**), we** reverse** the **subject-verb placement.** In **direct** sentences, we have the **verb before the subject**; while in** indirect,** the **verb follows the subject. **

questions.solution: It is clear that the sentence wants to convey that women empowerment is important or crucial. The option ‘necessary’ conveys this intended meaning and is thus the right answer.

questions.question: Racism is something we've all _______.
questions.solution: The meaning that is intended to be conveyed here is that racism is something we’ve all **seen or experienced**. The only option that closely resembles this meaning is ‘witnessed’.

questions.question: Many people _______ to believe that race isn’t a
questions.solution: Win or lose are both grammatically incorrect. Therefore they can be eliminated straightaway. Further, on reading the complete sentence in the paragraph, we ascertain that the word needed should negate the possibility of believing. Thus, they do not ‘learn’ to believe but ‘fail’ to believe.

questions.question: That race isn’t a _______ category
questions.solution: The meaning intended to be expressed here is that race is not something that a person receives through his physical attributes or genes. The only word that resembles the intended meaning is 'biological'.

questions.question: The _______ we make between races has nothing to do with
questions.solution: The intended meaning of the sentence is that the differences between races that people have come to create (has nothing to do with … so on). The key word being ‘differences’. Thus, 'distinction' is the correct answer.

questions.question: Race was created _______, primarily
questions.solution: It is clear that the author wishes to say that race is something an individual is not born with. It **i**s given to him by the society that he lives in. Thus the correct answer that conveys this intended meaning is ‘socially’.

questions.question: People _______ ideas and faces we
questions.solution: The author wants to convey that the society gives people a race based on what they come to understand about a person through their faces and ideas. Thus a word that denotes understanding or recognising is ‘perceive’.

questions.question: Changed _______ time, eventually adding groups
questions.solution: ‘Over’ is the adjective used to denote periodic change. Thus, 'changed over time' is the correct answer.

questions.question: Found the path for worldwide social _______ much
questions.solution: Reading the sentence from the paragraph, it is evident that the sentence is trying to highlight some of the races that found it difficult to be welcomed or accepted into the society. Thus, the correct answer is 'acceptance'.

questions.question: More ______. The irregular border of ethnicities touch
questions.solution: The sentence in the paragraph is referring to the fact that social acceptance for certain races was 'problematic or difficult'. Thus, the correct answer is difficult.

questions.question: Health and social mobility of people of _______.
questions.solution: The paragraph is primarily concerned with the issues of race which are denoted primarily by the colour or appearance of a person. The term 'colour' is often used interchangeably with race and is thus synonymous. The other options like gender, caste and creed are different concerns, but they are not addressed in this particular paragraph. Thus the answer is 'colour'.
